newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish pit trading barely mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish pit trading barely mixed.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished pit trading barely mixed but close to afternoon lows.
March Treasury bond futures dipped further as late trade picked up, touching the day's lowest level but leaving intact key support.
Some brokers tied the downtick to locals, saying those who had taken long positions when a dealer bought some 1,700 futures finally bailed out when the dealer finished buying and no upside resulted.
The contract remained above critical support technicians penciled as spanning the 111-00 to 111-05/32 zone.

Some brokers had wondered how March T-bonds would perform during the first fully staffed session of the new year and as Japan returned from an extended New Year's holiday to take in last week's three-point slide from a high at 114-06/32 to a low at 111-05/32 hit last Thursday.

Additional pressure stemmed from the dollar's decline, mainly against the yen after Japan's vice finance minister Tadashi Ogawa said overnight Monday that Japan will continue to deal appropriately with excessive forex moves, and that excessive yen weakness is not favorable for Japan's economy.
The remarks spooked a foreign exchange market that has been on the lookout for any signs that central banks might come to the beleaguered yen's rescue.

Floor brokers noted no response to comments by Atlanta Federal Reserve president Jack Guynn, who said on Monday that he expected foreign investors to continued as a source of demand for U.S. government securities.
He also said he expected U.S. gross domestic product to grow in 1997 by 2.0 percent to 2.5 percent while the inflation rate would remain little changed at around 3.0 percent.
In the short end, afternoon action dwindled after a morning seen dominated by hedging and swap-related activities, Eurodollar brokers said.

March T-bonds ended down 9/32 at 111-09/32, 10-year T-notes lost 3/32 to 108-15/32, muni-bonds fell 12/32 to 115-05/32, T-bills eased one bp to 94.92, and Eurodollars ended flat at 94.38. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
